name: Shiro gyaru

lead: Shiro gyaru (white gyaru) is the pale-skinned branch of gyaru, the Japanese fashion subculture known for bold makeup and dyed hair. Instead of the deep tan of ganguro, the look pairs fair skin with bleached blonde hair, elaborate false lashes and decorated nails.

The appearance payoff is a bright, high-contrast, doll-like face. It overlaps with the Japanese beauty ideal of fair skin (bihaku) and with the seiso gyaru style, and it is built from makeup, hair and lash techniques rather than a single product.

paras: Typical elements are a light matte base, silver or gold eyeshadow, upper and lower false lashes, circle contact lenses, drooping eyeliner, and bleached or pale hair, sometimes with teased volume. Nail art and coordinated Japanese fashion complete it.

Bleaching can dry and damage hair, circle lenses carry eye-health risks if poorly fitted or shared, and heavy makeup can irritate skin. These are general cosmetic risks rather than ones specific to the style.

chain: Pale matte base and no tan
Bleached blonde hair and large lashes
Circle lenses and light eye makeup
angle.text: The look changes appearance directly through makeup, lashes, lenses and hair colour. Followers build it from cosmetics and styling rather than treatments.

lead: Shiro gyaru, or white gyaru, is a gyaru look defined by pale skin, bleached blonde hair, elaborate lashes and nail art [1]. It is the fair-skinned counterpart to tan-focused looks such as ganguro, and people adopt it to create a bright, doll-like face with high-contrast features.

Gyaru, from the English 'gal', peaked in the Heisei era (1989-2019) and has seen a reported revival in the Reiwa era [1]. Shiro gyaru overlaps with seiso gyaru ('neat' or 'clean' gyaru), a name coined during the 2010s decline that Wikipedia says is interchangeable with it and tied to a revival of bihaku, the ideal of fair skin [1].
infobox: Heisei era; revival reported in Reiwa [1]

paras: Wikipedia places shiro gyaru among gyaru substyles, with pale skin, bleached blonde hair, elaborate lashes and nail art [1]. The broader gyaru makeup baseline described for the early 2010s includes matte foundation, silver or gold eyeshadow, dark lash lines, false lashes on both lids, circle lenses, pale cool-toned lips, drooping (tareme) liner, thin arched brows and eyelid tape for double eyelids [1].

Hair is heavily bleached or dyed, with teased gel-set volume known as sujimori, often built with extensions or wigs [1]. Reiwa-era versions use a lighter base, smaller lashes, thinner liner and more natural lenses [1].

Gyaru traces through the 1970s and 1980s into the kogal boom of the early 1990s, ganguro in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and hime gyaru in the early 2000s [1]. Shiro gyaru developed as the pale option beside tanned styles; seiso gyaru emerged in the 2010s as gyaru declined [1]. Social media has replaced print magazines as the main platform [1].

timeline.event: Kogal culture rises, followed by ganguro in the late 1990s [1].
Reported gyaru revival with lighter makeup [1].
